title: Automatically open option list in a `<select>` (`HTMLSelectElement`)

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
#### Problem

I am working on examples for some UIs that are using `<select>` (using [Storybook](https://storybook.js.org/)).

At least a few examples are intended to demonstrate how the `<select>` options are grouped and ordered. Those examples would benefit from a `<select>` being open straight away when user opens the example (since the point is to demonstrate the options).

However it seems there is no way to open a standard HTML `<select>` programmatically. Of course I can use a non-standard select, and that seems to be the main workaround the community is using, but I think longer-term default select should provide something.

#### Summary / TLDR

It would be good to have some way to open HTML `<select>` programmatically (either JS-only or HTML/JS).

#### Community Interest

* [StackOverflow: How can you programmatically tell an HTML SELECT to drop down (for example, due to mouseover)?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/249192/how-can-you-programmatically-tell-an-html-select-to-drop-down-for-example-due)
134 upvotes, 20 stars, top answer has 128 upvotes
* [StackOverflow: Is it possible to use JS to open an HTML select to show its option list?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/430237/is-it-possible-to-use-js-to-open-an-html-select-to-show-its-option-list)
143 upvotes, 9 stars
* _and [many more duplicates](https://www.google.com/search?q=select+element+open+site:stackoverflow.com) of the above_

#### Related Discussions

* #5792 might be related, but seems significantly wider in scope
* #2072 is similar but read only
